core_meaning.short_meaning: One who crushes bread for the people (during famine)
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Haashim is an Arabic-origin name meaning “One who crushes bread for the people (during famine)”.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: The name is the Arabic word itself, used unchanged as a given name rather than a derived or diminutive form.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Haashim corresponds to the Arabic form ہاشم (Arabic root ه ش م (h-sh-m); هاشم (Hāshim)). Its core sense is hashim; one who crushes (bread for the people). Haashim is Arabic هاشم (Hāshim), the byname of ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Manāf, great-grandfather of the Prophet, and the ancestor of the Hāshimite clan. The traditional explanation is 'one who crushes bread for the people (during famine)', from the root ه ش م 'to crumble, break'. The source gloss 'destroyer of evil' is unsupported and has been replaced.
